title: Video Generation Models Are General-Purpose Vision Learners
hook: Next-token prediction turned NLP into a generalist. This paper argues text-to-video generation can do the same for vision — one backbone, many tasks, beating specialists.
key_points: Argues text-to-video generation is vision's equivalent of next-token prediction: one pretraining paradigm, generalist visual intelligence.
GenCeption turns a pretrained video-diffusion backbone into one feed-forward model that performs many vision tasks steered by text instructions.
Matches or beats specialists (DepthAnything3, SAM3, VGGT-Omega, Sapiens, David) on depth, normals, camera pose, segmentation, 3D keypoints.
Outperforms alternative video-pretraining objectives (V-JEPA, VideoMAE) under matched settings.
Strikingly data-efficient: matches leading specialist models using 7-500x less training data.
Trained only on synthetic human videos, yet generalizes to real footage and out-of-distribution categories like animals and robots.
content_html: NLP's leap into generalist foundation models rode on one simple, scalable idea: predict the next token. This paper, from a team including Kaiming He, Andrew Zisserman, and Joao Carreira, argues computer vision has its own equivalent — large-scale text-to-video generation — and backs it with GenCeption, which turns a pretrained video-diffusion backbone into a single feed-forward perception system steerable by text instructions.
extra_html: Across depth estimation, surface normals, camera pose, expression-referring segmentation, and 3D keypoint prediction, GenCeption matches or beats specialized systems like DepthAnything3, SAM3, VGGT-Omega, Sapiens, and David — despite being one general model doing all of it. The video-generative backbone also beats alternative pretraining objectives such as V-JEPA and VideoMAE, and needs 7-500x less training data than leading task-specific models to reach comparable results. Most strikingly, a version trained only on synthetic human videos still generalizes to real footage and unfamiliar categories like animals and robots — evidence, the authors argue, that video generation is a foundational path to generalist vision intelligence, not just a synthesis tool.

related.title: Vision as Unified Multimodal Generation
related.hook: Detection, segmentation, depth, pose — each normally needs its own architecture. This model does all of them as text-and-image generation from one multimodal model, no task-specific heads.

related.title: Flex-Forcing: One Video Diffusion Model, Two Inference Modes
related.hook: Video diffusion models used to force a choice: globally coherent but slow, or fast streaming that drifts apart. Flex-Forcing chunks time and denoising steps together so one model does both.

flashcards.back_html: A feed-forward perception model built by repurposing a pretrained text-to-video diffusion backbone, steerable by text to perform many distinct vision tasks.

flashcards.prompt: How does GenCeption's data efficiency compare to specialist models like D4RT and VGGT-Omega?

choices.text: It matches their performance using 7-500x less training data
It needs roughly the same amount of training data
It requires 10x more training data but trains faster

flashcards.explanation_html: GenCeption's video-generative pretraining is exceptionally data-efficient, reaching comparable results with far less training data than specialist models.

flashcards.prompt: What surprising generalization did a GenCeption model trained only on synthetic human videos show?
flashcards.back_html: It generalized to real-world footage and out-of-distribution object categories it never saw in training, like animals and robots.

flashcards.prompt: What did GenCeption's video-generative backbone outperform under matched pretraining settings?

choices.text: Alternative video pretraining paradigms like V-JEPA and VideoMAE

flashcards.explanation_html: Under comparable settings, the video-generative pretrained backbone beat V-JEPA and VideoMAE, supporting generation as a stronger perception prior.
